transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Um... I guess I'm just having a hard time keeping up with things. Just... basic adult stuff. I keep forgetting to pay bills, or... returning emails for job interviews. I'll miss appointments, or just forget to follow through on errands. It's... it's starting to cost me real opportunities. So, that's why I'm here.
Have you been feeling down or depressed lately?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, I get frustrated, but... I don't think I'm depressed.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried a lot lately, even when there isn’t a clear reason for it?
No... not really. I mean, I worry about messing up and forgetting things, obviously, but... there's always a reason for it. So... no. Not just out of nowhere.
Have you had trouble staying focused or felt unusually restless or hyperactive, even when you're trying to get things done?

Yeah... I guess so. I mean, even without a job right now, I'm just... moving from one thing to the next all day. Like... I'll start laundry, or look at emails, reorganize my browser tabs... pace around, start dinner. 

I just... it's like I can't let myself stop. But... I don't actually finish any of it. So... yeah. I guess I'm restless.
How long have you felt this way about not being able to focus and feeling restless? Has this been happening since you were a child, or is it something that started more recently?

Um... a long time, I guess. Since I was little. 

Like... even back in elementary school, my teachers would write that I was bright, but... I don't know, I was always losing my worksheets. And... I'd rush through directions, or talk out of turn. My desk was always just... really messy. I could never find my assignments in there. 

So... yeah. It's not a new thing.

latest_inference.note: The patient's symptoms of inattention, restlessness, and disorganization have been present since childhood, which strongly supports a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive type. Other conditions such as depression, anxiety, and more recent onset stress-related disorders are ruled out due to the chronic, lifelong nature of the symptoms and absence of mood or anxiety symptoms as primary features.
